The test image shows soybean seeds. One seed (top left) appears healthy/tan, while the main seed has extensive dark brown-black fungal growth/mold covering the upper half of the seed surface. The texture appears crusty/moldy with dark discoloration on a tan base seed.

Key observations:
- Affected part: **seed**
- Color: dark brown/black mold covering upper portion of seed
- Texture: rough, crusty, moldy
- Candidates: Phomopsis (seed decay), Charcoal_Rot, Cercospora/Purple_Seed_Stain

Let me check the Phomopsis reference image.

The Phomopsis reference shows pod/stem lesions (cankers, circular spots on pods), which doesn't match the test image showing individual seed mold.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: individual soybean seeds, one with extensive dark brown/black crusty fungal growth covering the upper half of the seed
- The healthy seed (top left) is tan/normal for comparison
- The affected seed has dark, almost black, rough/granular mold texture

This is classic **Phomopsis** (Diaporthe) **seed decay** - one of the most common seed-specific manifestations, causing dark, moldy discoloration on soybean seeds. The Phomopsis reference happened to show pod symptoms, but seed decay is the other major presentation. The dark crusty coverage is characteristic of Phomopsis seed decay.
